title: Daily Temperatures
keyIdea: Keep a stack of days still waiting for a warmer day; their temperatures decrease from bottom to top (monotonic stack). A warmer day i pops every colder day on top and sets answer[prev] = i − prev, then waits itself. Each day is pushed and popped once: O(n).

approaches.name: Brute force: scan forward
approaches.idea: For each day, walk forward until a warmer day appears.
approaches.why: A falling run like 100, 99, 98, … makes every day scan to the end: ~n²/2 steps, ~5·10⁹ at n = 10⁵.

approaches.name: Monotonic stack
approaches.idea: For each day i: while the top day is colder, pop it and answer it with i − prev. Then push i.
approaches.why: Every index is pushed once and popped at most once, so all the while loops together do at most n pops. The stack can hold n days on a falling run.

quiz.q: Why does the stack store indices instead of temperatures?
options: The answer is a distance in days (i − prev), and the temperature is one lookup away

quiz.q: What's true about the temperatures on the stack, bottom to top?
options: They never go up (each waiting day is no warmer than the one below)

quiz.q: Why is it O(n) even with a while loop inside the for loop?
options: Each index is pushed once and popped at most once, so total pops ≤ n
The while loop runs at most once
